findings.message: parseDesignRequest re-decodes request.result against DesignResultSchema with the tighter DESIGN_LIMITS.resultBytes (1,048,576 bytes) cap, distinct from the outer DESIGN_LIMITS.requestBytes (1,114,112 bytes) cap already enforced on the whole request. The 65,536-byte gap between the two constants is sized to exactly the envelope overhead, so a request can pass the outer envelope check while its embedded result alone exceeds the tighter cap — this is the scenario this line exists to catch. No test in contracts.test.ts (or elsewhere in the design-review suite) constructs a 'result' phase request whose overall size is under requestBytes but whose result sub-object exceeds resultBytes, so this enforcement branch is unverified by any test; a regression that dropped or mis-sized this check would not be caught.
findings.rationale: This is a deliberately added, differently-sized bound (not a byproduct of the outer schema check) guarding an untrusted payload size; per the review's test-coverage mandate, a demonstrated gap in coverage for an asserted security/bound behavior is a reportable finding, not something excusable by execution being optional.

tasks.summary: Reviewed the checkpoint persistence (checkpoint.ts) and live progress/paging (progress.ts) primitives plus their fixture and test coverage at the pinned revisions. Atomic write (temp file 0600 + fsync + rename + directory fsync), bounded/no-follow load with identity/size/foreign checks, immutable-history enforcement on save, and metadata-only paged observation (no baseline/content retransmission, no activity renewal from polling) all match the stated acceptance checks and are exercised by the four tests, which pass on re-execution against the current (unmodified) checkout.

testCoverage.explanation: Read the full bodies of all four tests in checkpoint-progress.test.ts against the implementation they exercise. Each acceptance check maps to concrete assertions: (1) durable atomic write — rename-failure mock proves the prior file is byte-identical, the stray .tmp is cleaned from the directory listing, and file mode stays 0600; (2) fault handling — unauthenticated bounded no-follow load test exercises missing-file (undefined), corrupt JSON (preserved verbatim, load+save both reject), foreign project (rejects /identity/), oversized file (rejects /bounded regular/ before any read), and a symlinked checkpoint path (rejects via O_NOFOLLOW), plus a literal-only reviewId guard; (3) live polling — activity() distinguishes tool_started/tool_completed from a heartbeat (lastMeaningfulActivityAt unchanged across a heartbeat and across pure observation calls), and observeDesignCheckpoint never touches the tracker; (4) paging/no-leak — default poll returns empty completedResults and no 'reviewedContent' substring in the serialized output, cursor-paged poll returns exactly one result plus nextCompletedChunk, a used-up cursor returns empty, and an out-of-range cursor throws; (5) immutability/bounds — rewriting an already-accepted chunk's summary is rejected with /replace completed/, and a result inflated past the 1MiB per-chunk page limit is rejected on load with /page limit/. Re-ran the exact test file against the working tree (which has no uncommitted diff from the pinned commits) and all 4 cases passed, confirming the assertions hold against the real code, not just the diff.

testCoverage.explanation: Read the full bodies of all four tests in checkpoint-progress.test.ts against the implementation they exercise. Each acceptance check maps to concrete assertions: (1) durable atomic write — rename-failure mock proves the prior file is byte-identical, the stray .tmp is cleaned from the directory listing, and file mode stays 0600; (2) fault handling — unauthenticated bounded no-follow load test exercises missing-file (undefined), corrupt JSON (preserved verbatim, load+save both reject), foreign project (rejects /identity/), oversized file (rejects /bounded regular/ before any read), and a symlinked checkpoint path (rejects via O_NOFOLLOW), plus a literal-only reviewId guard; (3) live polling — activity() distinguishes tool_started/tool_completed from a heartbeat (lastMeaningfulActivityAt unchanged across a heartbeat and across pure observation calls), and observeDesignCheckpoint never touches the tracker; (4) paging/no-leak — default poll returns empty completedResults and no 'reviewedContent' substring in the serialized output, cursor-paged poll returns exactly one result plus nextCompletedChunk, a used-up cursor returns empty, and an out-of-range cursor throws; (5) immutability/bounds — rewriting an already-accepted chunk's summary is rejected with /replace completed/, and a result inflated past the 1MiB per-chunk page limit is rejected on load with /page limit/.
